title: You arrive full, and leave empty
note: The page's single arc from a filled point up to the standing at Arafah and down to an empty circle, a folded cloth at each end.

lines.text: You arrive full, and you leave empty
lines.sub: the same two cloths mark both ends

lines.text: Arafah, the ninth of Dhul Hijjah, the peak
A man in ihram wears two unstitched sheets
At the line, every marker is taken off
lines.sub: a citizen and a refugee, side by side

lines.text: The same clothing on the Day of Standing
You return as the day your mother bore you
lines.sub: the condition: no obscenity, no quarrel

lines.text: The circle is drawn empty on purpose
A newborn has no history: that is the gift
The sign is what changed afterwards
lines.sub: not what you felt while standing there

research.retell: The pilgrim arrives at Arafah in two plain white cloths carrying everything he owns, and leaves as the day his mother bore him, with a clean history to write on.
proof: you arrive, carrying everything; you return, carrying none of it
the standing at Arafah; 9 Dhul Hijjah. To Arafah after sunrise. Zuhr and Asr joined. Stand until sunset.
A man in ihram is dressed in two unstitched white sheets.; there is no way to tell a surgeon from a driver
Every marker a person spends his life assembling is taken off at a line in the desert.; a citizen of one country from a refugee of another
It is the same posture, the same clothing, the same crowd, the same helplessness, the same asking. The difference is that this time you chose to come, and you can still ask.

Whoever performs Hajj for Allah and does not speak obscenely nor act corruptly returns as the day his mother bore him.; Not forgiven a little. Not improved. Returned to the state of a newborn, who has never done anything at all.
The circle at the end of the arc is drawn empty on purpose: a newborn has no history, which is the gift, and also the problem, because a clean page has to be written on.
A newborn has no history. That is the gift
the scholars said the sign of an accepted Hajj is not what you felt at Arafah but what changed afterwards, and they said it because they had watched people come back unchanged.; The heart of it
